records: Go wherever the hell you want! You're more trouble than you're worth. You're fired!
The employer is angrily dismissing an uncooperative employee; preserve the hostility without inventing an offense.
Fine by me... Do what you like.
Al answers the dismissal with curt defiance rather than pleading for work.
What was that? A fight?
Charles speculates about the commotion; the fight is not established as a witnessed event.
He said he was fired... Was that man working as a bodyguard?
Hodram infers the former job from the dismissal, keeping it a question.
Tell me, who was that man?
Hodram directly asks the employer about the departing man.
Hm? Oh, him. Fighting's all he's good for. Wouldn't do as he was told, so I fired him. That's all.
Keep the employer's dismissive account as his own assessment, not an objective account of Al's character.
...Is he any good?
The short question refers to fighting skill in the preceding exchange.
Don't tell me you're interested in him. He's one hell of a fighter, I'll give him that. But is carrying a few bags really too much to ask?
Preserve both the exceptional fighting skill and the specific complaint about carrying luggage; do not replace it with generic insubordination.
Hmm... A perfect bodyguard, perhaps, but his personality leaves something to be desired. Too proud? Or just unable to work with others?
Charles offers competing explanations, not a settled diagnosis; his prim analysis sets up Hodram's dry retort.
I'm not sure you're one to talk about working with others, Charles. Come on.
Retain Hodram's pointed joke at Charles's expense and decision to follow Al.
What? Admiral, you're serious!?
Charles is surprised by Hodram's interest; retain the source-supported admiral address.
I want to speak to him myself before I decide.
Hodram wants a direct conversation rather than accepting the employer's assessment; no hiring decision has yet been made.
There he is. Quite a build, isn't he? Hard to miss.
Keep Charles's observation of Al's imposing physique, without adding a combat result.
Retain Hodram's silent appraisal before Al addresses him.
Want something?
Al opens brusquely, maintaining the guarded voice established during his dismissal.
You look like you've put a lot of work into that physique.
Hodram comments on Al's physical training; he is opening a conversation rather than making an offer yet.
That's obvious. And none of your business.
Keep Al's curt rejection of the overture.
Don't you understand? I approached you because I see promise in you. That attitude will cost you opportunities.
Hodram makes his interest explicit and challenges the self-defeating attitude; do not turn this into a demand for obedience.
What did you say!?
Al reacts angrily to the criticism.
I hear you've lost your job as a bodyguard. All that strength, and nothing to do with it.
Preserve the reported dismissal and Hodram's pointed inference about unused strength.
Looking to hire me? Who are you, anyway?
Al recognizes the employment approach and asks for Hodram's identity.
Then allow me to introduce myself. I'm {MACRO:FI}, an admiral of the Swedish Navy. I command a patrol fleet.
Preserve the exact name macro and explicit navy, admiral rank and patrol-fleet command; add no higher office.
An admiral, huh... I'm not interested in becoming a sailor.
Al acknowledges the rank but rejects seafaring work, not Hodram's nationality or character.
Is that all the judgment you have? You think I'd be a worse employer than the man who just fired you?
Hodram deliberately provokes Al by comparing himself with the former employer; preserve the persuasive challenge.
We only just met! Aren't you in a bit of a hurry?
Al objects to being rushed into a decision rather than denying the employer comparison outright.
A man loses respect when he can't make up his mind.
Retain the source's masculine-pride challenge in idiomatic English without adding a broader philosophy or rank.
Ghh...
Preserve Al's frustrated, wordless reaction to the challenge.
I can help you. If you want to come with me, decide now.
Critical direction: Hodram offers to help Al. Do not reverse this into Al helping Hodram or invent a specific promised benefit.
All right. I'll join your ship. Name's Al. Good to be aboard.
Keep the acceptance, self-introduction and courteous closing under Al's otherwise terse manner; retain established Al.
Hey, old man! Yeah, you! Old man!
Angelo's repeated rude address establishes his abrasive entrance; it is not a family relationship or a factual claim about Hodram's age.
Hodram turns his attention to the caller without an invented response.
That's right, you. Word down at the port is you're the admiral of this ship, right?
Keep Angelo's secondhand identification and overly familiar question.
I'm looking for work. Got a job for me on your ship, old man?
Preserve the job request and rude familiarity; do not add a proposed crew position.
What an insolent fellow... Shall we ignore him?
Gerhard's controlled disapproval precedes his later loss of temper.
Wait, Gerhard. I'm {MACRO:FI} {MACRO:FA}, captain of this ship.
Preserve both exact name macros and the source's captain role; use normal English name spacing rather than the Japanese separator.
You want to work aboard my ship? I've no use for dead weight in my fleet. What can you do?
Hodram tests the applicant's usefulness rather than rejecting him solely for his manners.
Mamma mia! Isn't it obvious? Strength and beauty. That's what I've got to offer!
Retain the conspicuous Italian exclamation and Angelo's boast about both fighting ability and appearance.
Unbelievable. Let's go. Men like this are usually all talk.
Gerhard dismisses the boast, setting up Angelo's actual skill in the duel.
Will you shut up? I'm talking to the gloomy old man here, not you!
暗い describes Hodram's gloomy demeanor, not complexion; preserve Angelo's insulting interruption.
That's quite enough! I'll put that strength of yours to the test. Draw!
Gerhard finally snaps and challenges him to a duel; no additional injury or lethal intent is added.
Just what I wanted. Come on!
Angelo welcomes the challenge with eager bravado.
Stop this!
Hodram tries to halt the confrontation before Gerhard insists.
Leave this to me! I can't let him insult you like that, Admiral!
Keep Gerhard's motive of defending Hodram's honor, not merely responding to a personal insult.
How do you like that? Told you I was strong!
Angelo boasts while pressing his advantage; do not imply he has won.
Grr...!
Preserve Gerhard's strained reaction before his eventual counter.
Well, well... I thought he was all talk, but he's giving even Gerhard trouble...
Hodram revises his initial assessment based on the fight; Gerhard has not yet been defeated.
Got you! This'll finish it!
Keep Angelo's premature confidence immediately before Gerhard counters.
Not good enough!
Gerhard's terse counter answers the overconfident attack.
Gah!
Retain Angelo's defeat reaction without naming an unsupported wound.
That's Gerhard for you. Still... There's something about this fellow.
Hodram recognizes Gerhard's victory but remains interested in Angelo's potential.
No way... I lost? That's a first...
Preserve Angelo's disbelief at his first defeat, not a claim about Gerhard's history.
It's a wide world. There are countless men as strong as you. Now then, shall we go, Admiral?
五万 is the idiom for countless here, not an exact count of fifty thousand; retain Gerhard's admonition and attempted departure.
You there. Want to join the ship?
Hodram unexpectedly renews the employment offer after Angelo loses.
W-what!?
Keep Gerhard's startled objection to the offer.
His manners need work, but he's got a real gift for swordsmanship. He's still raw, yet how many men have pushed you that hard?
Hodram balances acknowledged rudeness with demonstrated potential; preserve the argument directed at Gerhard.
Well... That's true, but...
Gerhard concedes the fighting ability while remaining reluctant.
Travel helps a man grow. I'm sure he'll change, too. What do you say?
Keep Hodram's belief in growth through travel; no guarantee of a particular training program is added.
Well, if you feel that strongly, {MACRO:FI}...
Gerhard reluctantly defers, preserving the exact captain-name macro without an invented additional title.
Hey... You really mean it? After the way I treated you?
Angelo's bravado gives way to surprise and recognition of his own rudeness.
Then you can make it up to us with your work.
Hodram offers a practical way to repay the rudeness; do not add a wage penalty or debt mechanic.
Heh... All right, I'll take you up on that. Thanks. I'm Angelo. Angelo Puccini.
Keep the accepted offer, warmer gratitude and exact established full name without making the abrasive character suddenly formal.
Say, Admiral. If you want to make real money trading, you can't keep puttering around the Mediterranean.
Angelo turns to blunt trade advice; this is a new conversational beat after recruitment.
Why is that?
Retain Hodram's request for an explanation.
Well, now! You know what you're talking about!
Julio approves the premise in his confident older voice; add no family address or military history.
Sure, the trade routes here are well established, so it looks promising. But the big powers have already developed everything. There isn't much profit left.
Preserve the contrast between developed routes and limited remaining opportunities; this is Angelo's economic explanation, not a new universal mechanic.
Hmm...
Keep Hodram's brief consideration rather than inserting a decision early.
You've got to head farther out. Africa and the New World still have plenty of room to grow. A little investment can bring a big return.
Preserve the two regions and investment potential; can expresses opportunity without guaranteeing all investments succeed.
And they've got unusual goods. Just hauling them back and forth to Europe should bring in a fortune.
Retain the unusual-goods explanation and the source's prediction rather than guaranteeing profits.
You know a great deal about trade, too. I wouldn't have guessed.
Hodram's surprise sets up Angelo's correction of where the advice came from.
Aw, come on. I'm just repeating what the sailors told me.
Critical attribution: Angelo credits sailors instead of claiming personal trading expertise.
Still, he's quite right.
Julio affirms the advice despite Angelo's admission that it is secondhand.
Even if you buy ships with more cargo holds, gaining market share in Europe is difficult. You can't trade large quantities at once without it.
Preserve the relation between cargo capacity, hard-to-gain market share and transaction size; do not invent an exact contract percentage here.
My thanks for the advice. We'll try heading out to the open sea.
Keep Hodram's appreciation and decision to explore trading farther afield, without naming an unstated immediate destination.
